# Ambuja Cements Limited

<!-- Generated by `make client-docs`. Do not edit inside the markers. -->

Researched 2026-09-29 · status **partial** · Budget spent: obtained a full Tier-1 statutory CSR annexure for FY2023-24 (from the Integrated Annual Report) plus identity/identifiers, but could not locate accessible Tier-1 CSR annexures for FY2022-23 (a 15-month transition period due to a fiscal-year-end change) or FY2021-22 within the search/document budget; several strong sources (MCA CSR-2 filing, BSE BRSR PDF, Prime Infobase CSR database, Scribd copies) were HELD/paywalled and were not routed around. Adani Foundation's role as implementing agency for Ambuja Cements is confirmed only via two undated Tier-4 news articles, not yet in a statutory filing. No project-level CSR spend table with amounts, no CSR-1 registration numbers for partners, and no discrete named-recipient grants were found for any of the three years.

Ambuja Cements Limited (CIN L26942GJ1981PLC004717, part of the Adani Portfolio since Sept 2022) is the Section 135-bound funder/filer entity researched here; it is kept as a separate record from Adani Foundation, which appears in two undated India CSR news articles as an on-ground implementing partner for specific Ambuja Cements community projects in Telangana (a school upgrade in Devapur, Adilabad district, and health camps in Nalgonda and Suryapet districts) — this is an implementing-agency/partner relationship, never a merge. Ambuja Cements also has its own long-standing CSR trusts (Ambuja Cement Foundation, Ambuja Vidya Niketan Trust, Ambuja Hospital Trust), distinct from Adani Foundation, documented as related-party CSR trusts in the FY2023-24 Integrated Annual Report. The statutory CSR Annexure in that report gives full Section 135 figures for FY2023-24: average net profit ₹2,562.75 crore, prescribed CSR ₹51.26 crore, ₹61.95 crore spent on projects plus ₹1.28 crore admin overheads for a total of ₹63.23 crore (an excess of ₹11.97 crore over obligation), with two third-party impact assessments completed (Taru Leading Edge for Rajasthan water projects in Pali and Nagaur districts; Thinkthrough Consulting for livelihood/SEDI/women's-empowerment SROI work in Howrah district, West Bengal). FY2022-23 and FY2021-22 statutory annexures were not retrieved within budget; Ambuja changed its fiscal year-end from December to March around 2022-23 (reporting a 15-month transition period), complicating clean Apr-Mar mapping for those years, and the relevant filings (MCA CSR-2, Prime Infobase database copy of the FY2022-23 CSR report, BSE-hosted BRSR PDF) were either paywalled, HELD by robots.txt, or not located.

Website: https://www.ambujacement.com

- footprints in plant-adjacent districts (Himachal Pradesh, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh)
- stated priority geography kept separate from footprint
- partners including Adani Foundation as implementing agency, and Ambuja's own CSR trusts
- programs/themes, metrics (SROI, beneficiaries), contacts (CSR committee), documents
